# docker container
jasonrivers/nagios:latest

# log file location 
log_file=/opt/nagios/var/nagios.log

# Add Host Configuration
This configuration file could be placed in /opt/nagios/etc/objects/ or within a separate file under /opt/nagios/etc/objects/hosts/ (for better organization).

define host {
    use             linux-server          ; Host template
    host_name       vc-ps-fit-chewy-08    ; Unique host name
    address         10.74.135.70         ; IP address of the server
    check_command   check-host-alive     ; Command to check host status
}

For monitoring SSH on vc-ps-fit-chewy-08:
define service {
    use                     generic-service     ; Service template
    host_name               vc-ps-fit-chewy-08  ; The host this service belongs to
    service_description     SSH Check           ; Description of the service being monitored
    check_command           check_by_ssh!remlab@10.74.135.70!/usr/lib/nagios/plugins/check_ping -H 10.74.135.70 -w 100.0,20% -c 200.0,50%
}

# Organize Configuration Files
configure the *.cfg in the nagios.cfg (/opt/nagios/etc)
cfg_file=/opt/nagios/etc/objects/vc-ps-fit-chewy-08.cfg


#  Configure SSH Access (for agentless monitoring)
•	Make sure the Nagios server can SSH into the target host (vc-ps-fit-chewy-08) using the remlab user.
•	Set up passwordless SSH access (SSH key authentication) between the Nagios server and the monitored host:
•	ssh-copy-id remlab@10.74.135.70
•	Verify SSH access from the Nagios server to the new host:
•	ssh remlab@10.74.135.70

#  Ensure Plugins are Available
Ensure the appropriate plugins are available on the Nagios server, particularly check_by_ssh and any other plugins you want to use (e.g., check_ping, check_http, etc.).
Verify the plugin location:
ls /usr/lib/nagios/plugins/check_by_ssh
or
ls /opt/nagios/libexec/check_by_ssh


# Verify the Configuration
Before restarting Nagios, verify that the configuration files are valid:
/opt/nagios/bin/nagios -v /opt/nagios/etc/nagios.cfg
This will check for syntax errors in the configuration files.

# Restart Nagios
After adding the new host and service definitions, restart Nagios to apply the changes:
kill -HUP $(pidof nagios)
Or:
/opt/nagios/bin/nagios -d /opt/nagios/etc/nagios.cfg

# Check Nagios Web Interface
Go to the Nagios web interface (http://<nagios-server-ip>:8080) to check that the new server and services are being monitored correctly. You should see the status for the new host and services on the web interface.


Summary Checklist:
1.	Host Configuration: Add a define host block for the new server.
2.	Service Configuration: Add a define service block for each service (e.g., SSH) to monitor.
3.	SSH Access: Ensure passwordless SSH access to the new server for agentless monitoring.
4.	Plugins: Ensure Nagios plugins are installed and available on the server.
5.	Configuration File Organization: Add new configurations to appropriate files and directories.
6.	Validate and Restart Nagios: Validate configuration and restart Nagios.
7.	Web Interface Check: Verify the status of the new host and services in the Nagios web interface.
